claims.text: Wheat-noodle ramen/tanmen, wheat-skin gyoza and wonton, and wheat-based soy seasonings are all prepared in a single small shared kitchen, so heavy gluten cross-contact is unavoidable.
Broths and stir-fries are seasoned with soy-based (wheat-containing) sauce; the chashu ramen uses a soy-seasoned chicken stock.
Kitchen centers on pork (housemade chashu) and a multi-hour chicken stock; even vegetable dishes like the tanmen are cooked in the same broth/seasoning system and are not documented as animal-free.
Menu is built on oden and wheat udon; the shared simmering dashi and many oden items contain soy sauce (wheat) and fish stock, so cross-contact with gluten is inherent.
Oden broth in this style is seasoned with regular soy sauce, which contains wheat; no wheat-free tamari is documented.
All oden items share one pot of fish/bonito dashi alongside eggs, fishcakes and meat, so any item carries animal-broth cross-contact.
The plate includes fried pakoda fritters and crisp lentil papad/appalam, which commonly involve wheat or shared frying oil; no gluten-free protocol is documented.
Curries on most days include fish, mutton, chicken or pork options served from the same daily lineup as the vegetable curry; sides' use of ghee/dairy or any stock is not published.

The fixed meals format includes a wide range of vegetable sides (coconut carrots, mustard yam and taro, dal, kachumbar salad, pickles, chutneys) so a largely plant-based plate can usually be assembled.

name: とろけるハンバーグ 福よし ならまち店 (Torokeru Hamburg Fukuyoshi Naramachi-ten)

claims.text: Diners finish cooking the wagyu patty themselves on a tabletop iron griddle, and garlic rice is fried afterward in the same meat juices/pan, creating shared-surface cross-contact risk for anyone avoiding gluten.

A wasabi-soy-sauce condiment is offered alongside the hamburg, and a house steak sauce is served; soy sauce typically contains wheat and the wheat content of these sauces should be confirmed with staff.
Every main centers on wagyu beef and even the garlic rice is cooked in beef drippings, so there are no vegan-safe preparations.
The official menu instructs guests to ask staff about any allergens not listed, indicating allergen handling is by direct inquiry rather than a published program.
The hamburg patty is made from 100% domestic black wagyu with no binders, so the patty itself uses no wheat flour, egg, or dairy.
The bento and kaiseki include simmered dishes and clear soups that conventionally use Japanese soy sauce (which contains wheat) and fish/kombu dashi; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
The chagayu bento includes animal items such as chicken wrapped in burdock and egg crepe, and dishes commonly use fish dashi, so plant-based diners cannot assume the set is vegan.

name: とよのあかり すずの音 (Toyonoakari Suzunone)

claims.text: Wheat is pervasive: the signature hot pot includes fried tofu, tsukune, and shrimp crackers, and lunch sets use Miwa sōmen and ramen (wheat noodles); no gluten-free handling is documented.
As a Japanese izakaya/sake house, seasonings rely on standard soy-sauce-based and chicken-dashi preparations; no wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned.
The standard 草鍋 broth is chicken-based and includes Yamato chicken and tsukune; even vegetable-forward orders are prepared in a kitchen centered on chicken and dashi.
Strong focus on locally grown Yamato vegetables, with a salt-plum vegetable-umami broth option for the hot pot and staff who explain the day's produce to guests.

name: トラットリア・ピアノ (Trattoria Piano)

claims.text: Core menu is wood-fired pizza and fresh pasta, so wheat flour is central to the kitchen and airborne/surface flour cross-contamination is effectively unavoidable. No gluten-free menu or accommodations are documented.

Pizzas and pastas typically involve cheese, butter, and eggs, and meat dishes use Nara brand meats; shared oven and prep surfaces mean cross-contact with animal products is likely. No vegan menu is documented, so confirm each dish with staff.

Strongly vegetable-forward for an Italian restaurant, with Yamato traditional vegetables featured prominently and a dedicated vegetable-heavy 'Pizza Yamato', so plant-leaning diners have real options to discuss.

name: 月日亭 近鉄奈良駅前店 (Tsukihitei Kintetsu Nara Ekimae-ten)

claims.text: Kitchen routinely prepares wheat-batter tempura and soy-sauce/dashi-based dishes; no gluten-free protocol is documented, so cross-contamination should be assumed.
Sukiyaki and kaiseki dishes rely on standard soy sauce and dashi, which contain wheat; no wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned.
Menu is built around beef, pork and chicken and fish-based dashi; even the chagayu set includes non-vegan sides such as prosciutto-wrapped cheese.
